problems.title: Operator norms do not lower-bound every directional gain
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, PDF p.4, paragraph before Remark 1
claim: Section 3.1 uses a restoration Jacobian norm above one to infer amplification of slight input changes, then invokes a larger detector norm.
analysis: Take \(A=\operatorname{diag}(2,1/10)\) and \(M=\operatorname{diag}(20,1/10)\). Their operator norms are \(2\) and \(20\), but the cascade maps \(\epsilon e_2\) to \((\epsilon/100)e_2\). These smooth linear maps therefore contract that finite perturbation despite large maximum gains.
result: Necessary amplification in every direction does not follow. Existence of amplified directions and the empirical observations remain possible.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: The valid upper bound is \(\operatorname{Lip}(D\circ R)\leq\operatorname{Lip}(D)\operatorname{Lip}(R)\). A particular first-order gain is \(\|J_DJ_Rv\|/\|v\|\); a universal local lower bound requires a minimum-singular-value condition.
problems.impact_rationale: This corrects a qualitative necessity claim, without invalidating the main empirical result.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Training-point alignment does not control the global envelope
problems.source_location: Section 4.1, Remark 3, PDF p.6; Appendix A, PDF p.13
claim: Remark 3 assumes restoration-gradient alignment at a training point \(x^\star\), then bounds the derivative of the global Jacobian maximum \(C(\theta)\).
analysis: For \(B_\theta(x)=x+\theta(x^2-x)\) on \([0,1]\), \(0<\theta<1/2\), use losses \(L_r=2-\theta\), \(L_d=3-2\theta\), and weight \(1\). Then \(g_r=-1\), \(g_d=-2\), and at training point \(x^\star=0\) the required alignment is \(1\). Nevertheless \(C(\theta)=1+\theta\), attained at \(x=1\). Gradient flow has \(\dot\theta=3\), so \(\dot C=3\), while the printed bound is \(1\). Correcting only the detection-term sign does not repair the missing maximizer condition.
result: The stated sufficient condition does not establish this ancillary stability bound. It does not refute improved performance of the joint model.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Under the usual compactness and differentiable-envelope conditions, require alignment at every active maximizer. Use the signed detection contribution \[\max_{x\in\arg\max\phi}[-\langle\nabla_\theta\phi,g_d\rangle]\]. Strict decrease needs this term to be smaller than the restoration contribution.
problems.impact_rationale: The counterexample rejects one supporting remark; a central experimental failure is not demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Public losses differ from the displayed parameter-Jacobian objective
problems.source_location: Section 4.2, Remark 4 and full objective, PDF p.7; Table 4, PDF p.9; released loss path
claim: Section 4.2 uses \(L_d+\lambda L_r+\lambda_p\|\nabla_\theta f_\theta(x)\|\), with a Charbonnier restoration loss and stated weights \(\lambda=10\), \(\lambda_p=0.01\).
analysis: The public recipes assemble weighted absolute-error/perceptual reconstruction terms and clipping or loss-gradient penalties. A loss-gradient norm is not generally the model-output parameter-Jacobian norm in the equation; clipping is an optimizer operation rather than that objective. No configuration-to-table mapping establishes which historical experiment used these recipes.
result: The inspected recipe is insufficient to reproduce the exact displayed objective. No published table entry is numerically contradicted.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Provide the exact loss, norm, reduction and experiment configuration. An operator norm must not silently become a Frobenius estimator; implementing another regularizer requires its own interpretation and evaluation.
problems.impact_rationale: This is release-to-description correspondence with unresolved historical attribution.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
